docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:13:# Phantom-SoM Pre-Registration (Draft)
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:15:> **Status: draft** — pending advisor sync lock. Once advisor signs (single-line email or co-authored commit), `status` flips to `locked`, `registered_git_sha` records the commit at lock time, and `witnessed_by` records advisor name + lock timestamp. `data_lock_until` records when 16-cell rerun finishes — between lock-time and completion-time, NO additional analyses may be added to gating-family tests.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:30:1. **Phantom-SoM is the deployment hero**: 4-fold drop-in property (cost ≈ DOM, latency ~50% lower, signal AUROC ≥ baseline, drop-one positive) is the headline practical contribution. This is pre-registered strict.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:32:2. **Phantom space is a structural claim, not a 3-arm deployment claim**: P-text and P-prompt are not pre-registered as deployment-grade routing arms. They are pre-registered as **structural ablation evidence** validating that phantom space (the cube image-off half) is a 2-axis multi-region empirical structure rather than collapsed to the single P-SoM point.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:48:#### H1 — Hero deployment claim (P-SoM is hidden routing arm)
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:50:P-SoM drop-one > 0 across cells, satisfying ALL three sub-conditions:
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:53:- **H1(ii)** ≥ K_h1 of N_cells individually Holm-significant at α=0.05 within the per-cell P-SoM sub-family (m = N_cells), where **K_h1 = 0.75** (commit-locked, see §4).
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:56:#### H2 — 4-fold drop-in property (P-SoM specifically)
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:60:- **(a) Cost** — median cost(P-SoM) within ±10% of median cost(DOM); reflects the by-construction property that `[SOM_MARKS]` is an AXTree regex filter (no image embedding tokens). Tested empirically per cell.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:61:- **(b) Latency** — median latency(P-SoM) ≤ 0.6 × median latency(SoM); reflects skipping image inference stage. Tested empirically per cell.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:62:- **(c) Signal AUROC** — top-1 routing-signal AUROC(P-SoM) ≥ AUROC(DOM) − 0.05 (within 5pp). Tested empirically per cell, signal selected per `aggregate_routing_auroc.py` top-1.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:63:- **(d) Drop-one magnitude** — folded into H1(iii); P-SoM contributes ≥ 1.0pp lift on average.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:67:Each phantom-space axis (axis 1 = text payload via P-text; axis 2 = SoM-style prompt via P-prompt) contributes tasks NOT solved by P-SoM, evidencing axis decomposition is empirically non-trivial (i.e., phantom space is a multi-region 2D structure, not a collapsed 0D point):
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:69:- **H3(i)** axis 1: |P-text ∖ P-SoM| unique-count > 0 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0 in ≥ K_h3 of N_cells.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:70:- **H3(ii)** axis 2: |P-prompt ∖ P-SoM| unique-count > 0 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding 0 in ≥ K_h3 of N_cells.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:73:K_h3 = 0.67 (commit-locked, see §4). This is **lower** than K_h1 because the structural claim is weaker than the deployment claim — non-overlap existence is sufficient, deployment-grade magnitude is not required.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:104:#### H7 — Tier 1 oracle router lift over best-single-mode baseline (offline supervised)
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:106:Tier 1 router: TF-IDF task-instruction features + binary task features (`has_ref_image`, `has_finish_string_match`) → logistic regression predicting best-mode-per-task. Trained per cell-fold (site-stratified k-fold). Lift = adjusted-SR(router) − adjusted-SR(best-single-mode-baseline) per cell.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:114:- Best-single-mode-baseline = mode with highest mean adjusted-SR on train fold per cell, evaluated on held-out test fold (no test leak).
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:122:Tier 2 router: features extracted from agent's first-step observation (task instruction + initial DOM/SoM observation slice + initial action diversity proxy) → predicts which mode to commit for full trajectory. **No test leak**: features use only first-step info, mode commitment thereafter is fixed.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:124:- **H8(i)** Tier 2 router lift over Tier 1 oracle baseline ≥ 0 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding −1.0pp (paper claims Tier 2 ≈ Tier 1 within deployment-grade tolerance, given Tier 2 is leak-free and deployment-realistic).
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:125:- **H8(ii)** Tier 2 router lift over best-single-mode-baseline ≥ 1.0pp, ≥ K_h1 cells Holm-significant.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:137:| **R1** | H1 holds AND H2 (a)(b)(c) all hold AND H3(i) holds AND H3(ii) holds | "Phantom routing space (M1/M2 2-axis empirical structure); P-SoM as deployment hero, P-text/P-prompt as structural ablation arms validating axis decomposition." | STRONGEST |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:138:| **R2** | H1+H2 hold AND only one of H3(i)/(ii) holds | "Phantom routing space (single-axis empirical structure) with P-SoM as deployment hero; remaining axis decomposition theoretical (Zoom 1 architectural argument only)." | MODERATE-STRONG |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:139:| **R3** | H1+H2 hold AND neither H3(i)/(ii) holds | "Phantom-SoM is hidden 4th routing arm; M1/M2 axis decomposition supported by Zoom 1 architectural argument only, not empirically validated by ablation." | MODERATE (= 04-30 fallback) |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:140:| **R4** | H1 holds AND H2 partially fails (e.g., (a) cost or (b) latency fails on some site) | "Phantom-SoM partial drop-in" + §4 disclosure of failed sub-claim. | WEAK; substantial revision |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:149:- H1(ii) per-cell P-SoM Holm: m = N_cells.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:164:- H8(ii) Tier 2 vs best-single-mode-baseline: m = N_cells.
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:196:| **Cell inclusion (main)** | Phase A post-fix only (commit ≥ 3c15cd7) | bug-clean rerun |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:198:| **N inclusion floor** | ≥ 100 ep per (cell × mode) | Statistical power baseline |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:202:| **Mode operational definitions** | 6 modes per paper §3 (text format × prompt × image): DOM (AXTree+DOM-prompt+no image) / SoM ([SOM_MARKS]+SoM-prompt+image) / Vision (no text+image) / P-text ([SOM_MARKS]+DOM-prompt+no image) / P-prompt (AXTree+SoM-prompt+no image) / P-SoM ([SOM_MARKS]+SoM-prompt+no image) | Stipulative — **no post-hoc episode reclassification**. Episodes systematically excluded per (FP filter / N-floor / data-corruption flag), never redefined which mode they belong to. Edge cases (empty AXTree / 0 marks / OCR-empty) follow `condition_meta.json` declared mode |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:207:| **Best-single-mode baseline (H7/H8 anchor)** | Per cell: mode with highest mean adjusted-SR on train fold | Used as comparison anchor for router lift; **train/test split-stratified** to prevent test leak |
docs/checkpoints/pre_run/preregistration.md:209:| **Stopping rules / contamination halt criteria** (audit B7) | (a) **Pre-launch**: `make pre-launch-check` validates seed configured + HF SHA pinned + git working tree clean + GPU available + disk free > 20GB; failure halts launch (per audit C10). (b) **Smoke-test gate**: first 10 episodes per cell must show ≥ 1 success (or ≥ 1 N/A by ua_match) AND auth-state `logged_in=True`; otherwise halt + watchdog auth_refresh + restart, log incident in `master_bug_catalog.md`. (c) **Auth/site contamination halt**: ≥ 5 consecutive episodes with `not_logged_in` ⇒ stop cell, refresh auth, archive partial run as `_dirty_partial`, restart fresh. (d) **Eval drift halt**: if rerun on identical archived episode produces SR delta > 5pp via `validate_run.py --strict`, freeze cell + investigate evaluator code. (e) **OOM / hardware halt**: 3 consecutive job failures ⇒ stop cell, document hardware in incident log, manually re-queue with diagnostic output. | Halt rules protect data purity; halted cells restarted only after root-cause documented in `master_bug_catalog.md` + bug fix committed. Lock 2026-05-09. |

codex
Design has 6 paper-grade flaw(s) — must fix before launch.

**Confirmed Design Flaws**
1. **Layer: orchestrator / cell-scope**
   **Evidence:** `preregistration.md:196` locks main inclusion to “Phase A post-fix only”; `run_manifest.yaml:8-16` says pre-fix and post-fix siblings cannot be mixed; but `queue_16cell_paper_grade.sh:22-28` launches only phantom cells, not DOM/SoM/Vision baseline siblings.
   **Impact:** H1 drop-one, §4 hero tables, forest plots, and cost/latency comparisons need same-vintage baselines. As written, the rerun may produce fresh phantom arms compared against archived pre-fix baselines or no paper-grade baselines.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** hours. Either rerun required baseline modes too, or explicitly redefine the 16-cell rerun as phantom-only and document where post-fix DOM/SoM/Vision come from.

2. **Layer: preregistration / framing-rule**
   **Evidence:** `preregistration.md:50-54` says H1 requires pooled meta, K_h1 cells, and TOST; `preregistration.md:69-73` says H3 requires K_h3 cells; `preregistration.md:137-141` says R5 fires if pooled meta fails or `< K_h1`; but `preregistration.md:211` says K_h1/K_h3 are “secondary transparency checks, not gates.”
   **Impact:** The paper’s pass/fail function is internally contradictory. A reviewer can say the preregistration was amended after power analysis to de-gate an inconvenient criterion.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** 1-2 hours, but must be done before witness lock. Pick one: K gates claims, or K is transparency-only. Then rewrite H1/H3/R1-R5/§6 consistently.

3. **Layer: methodology drift / actual decision rule**
   **Evidence:** prereg H1 is “P-SoM drop-one > 0” (`preregistration.md:50`); prereg H3 is P-text/P-prompt unique tasks not solved by P-SoM (`preregistration.md:67-70`). But `preregistration_decision_test.py:29-32` defines H1 as “Phantom-SoM ≥ best DOM/SoM/Vision” and H3 as “Drop-one oracle lift from Phantom-SoM”; implementation matches that at `:83-120`.
   **Impact:** The post-run “preregistration decision” table would not test the preregistered H1/H3. This is direct preregistration-vs-actual mismatch.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** hours. Rename the script output as a transparency diagnostic, or align the script and paper table to prereg H1/H3.

4. **Layer: paper-prose / mode definition**
   **Evidence:** prereg defines 6 modes including P-prompt (`preregistration.md:202`) and H3 axis 2 depends on P-prompt (`preregistration.md:67-70`). Advisor sync also frames P-prompt as a phantom corner (`ADVISOR_SYNC.md:48-55`). But current paper §3 excludes AXTree+SoM prompt: “intentionally excluded from Paper 1” (`section3_definition.md:56-67`), and §4 reports only five modes with no P-prompt (`section4_empirical_findings.md:11-19`).
   **Impact:** The strongest R1 “2-axis phantom space” hook cannot be supported by the current §3/§4 prose. It either tests P-prompt or it doesn’t.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** 30-60 min prose/spec edit, plus confirm analysis tables include P-prompt where H3 needs it.

5. **Layer: cell-scope / witness**
   **Evidence:** prereg says final scope is 16 cells with shop × 2 phantom arms (`preregistration.md:206`); queue agrees (`queue_16cell_paper_grade.sh:22-28`); `next_steps.md:101-106` agrees. But advisor follow-up says “B0 × {cls,red,shop} × 3 phantom + B1 × {cls,red,shop} × 3 phantom” while calling it 16 cells (`advisor_sync_5_5_followup.md:11`), which arithmetic implies 18. OSF manifest repeats a 16/18 ambiguity in the note (`osf_lock_manifest.md:47`).
   **Impact:** Advisor witness could lock the wrong denominator. K_h1=12 and K_h3=11 only mean what they claim if N=16 and shop P-prompt is explicitly excluded.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** minutes. Fix the email/follow-up and OSF manifest before sending or receiving witness confirmation.

6. **Layer: preregistration / stopping rule**
   **Evidence:** `preregistration.md:209` says first 10 episodes per cell must show ≥1 success or ≥1 N/A, otherwise halt, refresh, and restart. Follow-up itself expects low-power B1 shop outliers (`advisor_sync_5_5_followup.md:152-154`).
   **Impact:** This is outcome-dependent stopping/restart. For a true 5-10% SR cell, “no success in first 10” is common. Discarding/restarting on that condition can bias low-SR cells upward or make valid cells unlaunchable.
   **Severity:** HIGH.
   **Defuse effort:** 30-60 min. Make smoke gate depend on auth/artifact/evaluator health only, or run smoke tasks outside the registered data.

**Probable Concerns**
- **TOST target/unit ambiguity:** H1 uses δ=1.0pp for drop-one magnitude (`preregistration.md:54`), H2 cost says ±10% (`:60`), advisor follow-up says TOST δ tests cost equivalence (`advisor_sync_5_5_followup.md:178-183`), and decision script computes relative cost percent (`preregistration_decision_test.py:152-163`). Needs cleanup before lock.
- **Router family unresolved:** H7/H8 are pending advisor lock (`preregistration.md:102-127`), intro says learned routing is deferred (`section1_intro.md:13`), while ADVISOR_SYNC leans paper-1 primary (`ADVISOR_SYNC.md:146`). Fine if deferred; dangerous if §6 claims remain.
- **Heterogeneity rule conflict:** `preregistration.md:210` says I² >75% means “do not pool,” while H1(i) depends on pooled random-effects significance. Need a rule for R1-R5 if heterogeneity forbids pooling.

**Methodology Drift**
- Canonical prereg H1: pooled P-SoM drop-one >0 + magnitude ≥1pp.
- Actual decision script H1: P-SoM single-mode SR ≥ best baseline.
- Paper prose H1-ish: “independent routing arm” carried by four-arm drop-one on B0 cls/red.
- Which is right: prereg H1 should be canonical. Defuse by rewriting the decision script/table labels and final §4 claims around drop-one, not single-mode best-baseline wins.

**Reviewer Ammunition**
1. Why is the “16-cell rerun” not rerunning DOM/SoM/Vision if drop-one uses those baselines? Current answer: no clean answer prepared.
2. Is K-of-N a gate or not? Current answer: contradictory docs.
3. Why is P-prompt required for H3 but excluded in §3? Current answer: contradictory docs.
4. Why does the advisor email say all sites × 3 phantom if queue skips shop P-prompt? Current answer: doc error, must fix.
5. Is δ=1pp a success-rate margin or a cost-equivalence margin? Current answer: contradictory docs.
6. Does a first-10 success smoke rule bias low-performing cells? Current answer: yes, unless changed before lock.
7. Are learned-router claims in paper 1? Current answer: intro says no; prereg leaves pending.
8. What happens if I² says “do not pool” but H1 pooled meta is significant? Current answer: no explicit R-rule branch.

**What I Read**
- Full preregistration: ~20 min.
- Paper planning §1-3 and relevant later risk/router sections: ~12 min.
- Paper §1/§3/§4/limitations: ~12 min.
- Advisor sync + follow-up: ~8 min.
- Queue, checklist, next_steps, CLAUDE hard rules, preflight: ~10 min.
- Cell frontmatter + manifest: ~10 min.
- Historical audits: summary/confirmed-bug portions only, as requested. I did not reread the full 130k-token codex audit body or all bug catalog entries.

**Verdict On Next Steps**
Delay launch. These are not post-data disclosure fixes because several affect what data must be collected and what the locked decision function means.

The one thing to fix tonight: make a single canonical launch/prereg bundle that answers “what cells are being run and what tests do they gate?” Include baseline-vintage policy, 16 vs 18 scope, P-prompt inclusion, K gate status, and TOST units. After that, the advisor email can witness a coherent spec.
